questions.question: Describe the main structural members of a cell phone tower from the ground up and state the job of each.
questions.expected_answer: A solid concrete foundation with bolts anchors the feet. Legs, three or four sloping steel members, carry the weight of the tower and antennas to the foundation and resist being lifted on the windward side and pushed down on the leeward side. Horizontals hold the legs apart at a fixed distance. Diagonals join horizontals and legs, dividing each panel into triangles so the frame cannot distort. The head frame at the top carries panel and dish antennas, cables run down to cabinets at the base, and tall thin masts may be braced by guy wires anchored to the ground.

questions.question: Explain what triangulation is and why it is essential in a tall frame structure exposed to wind.
questions.expected_answer: Triangulation is dividing a frame into triangles by adding diagonal members. A rectangular panel with pinned corners can lean into a parallelogram under a sideways push without any member changing length, so a tower of rectangles would sway and collapse. A triangle cannot change shape unless a side changes length, so a diagonal locks the panel: to lean, the wind would have to stretch or squash steel. Crossing diagonals ensure one is always in tension whichever way the wind blows, allowing thin members, so the tower is rigid yet light.

questions.question: Compare an electricity pylon, a farm wind pump and mine headgear, identifying the load each carries and the structural lesson they share.
questions.expected_answer: A pylon carries high-voltage cables, and its main load is the sideways pull of the heavy cables and the wind on them, so it is heavier and guyed at corners of the line. A wind pump supports a spinning wheel and tail vane and drives a pump rod, and its load is the vibrating, changing push of wind on the wheel, so it is strongly tapered and bolted to concrete footings. Headgear carries the winding wheels over a mine shaft, and its load is the weight of the cage and ore plus the pull of the winding cable, so it is a massive frame with a sloping back leg. All three are tall frames that are triangulated, tapered and anchored.
